title: Security Enablement Appendix — Standard Slide Notes (Encryption, Audit Logging, SSO/RBAC, Data Residency, Compliance Overview)
author: Soojin Lee
content:
## Purpose
These slide notes are the standardized, Security-approved speaker notes and on-slide guidance for security-focused customer decks (typically appended to the end of the standard Redwood Inference deck).

Use these slides to:
- Answer the “top 5” security review questions consistently (encryption, audit logging, SSO/RBAC, data residency, compliance program).
- Clarify Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private shared responsibility boundaries.
- Avoid over-committing beyond what is contractually guaranteed or currently shipped.

These notes are written to be **safe-by-default** for external presentation. If a customer requests evidence artifacts (SOC 2 report, pen test summary, detailed architecture diagrams), route to the evidence request process via Security/GRC.

---

## How to use this appendix
### When to include
- Late-stage deals: security review initiated, procurement engaged, or “security posture” is a decision criterion.
- Regulated prospects evaluating VPC/on-prem (Private) or dedicated isolation (Dedicated).

### How to present
- Keep on-slide text concise; use the speaker notes for detail.
- Anchor on shared responsibility: “What Redwood provides” vs “What the customer controls.”
- If you don’t know: do not speculate. Say: “We can confirm in writing via our Security team and share the relevant one-pager / approved RFP language.”

### Words/claims to avoid (unless explicitly confirmed in the deal context)
- Avoid absolute terms: “always,” “never,” “no access,” “fully isolated,” “zero retention.”
- Avoid timelines: “within X hours” for incident notification unless it is in the executed agreement.
- Avoid roadmap commitments (feature delivery dates, upcoming certifications).

### Standard footer for all appendix slides
- “Redwood Inference — Security Enablement Appendix (v2) — Last reviewed: 2026-02-12”
- “For evidentiary materials, request via Security/GRC (NDA may be required).”

---

## Slide 1 — Compliance & Security Program Overview
### Recommended slide title
**Security Program Overview (Compliance, Assurance, Operations)**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- Security program with dedicated Security Engineering + GRC oversight
- Third-party assurance (SOC 2 report available under NDA)
- Secure SDLC, vulnerability management, and incident response processes
- Deployment options: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on‑prem)

### Speaker notes (approved framing)
- “We operate a formal security and compliance program designed for enterprise procurement and regulated workloads. For assurance, we can provide our SOC 2 report under NDA through our GRC process.”
- “We follow a secure development lifecycle: peer review, CI controls, dependency scanning, and a structured vulnerability remediation process.”
- “Operationally, we have defined incident response procedures and customer communication pathways. Contract language governs notification timelines; we avoid making blanket timing claims in slideware.”

### If asked: “Are you SOC 2 Type II certified?”
- Use: “We can share our current SOC 2 report under NDA and walk you through scope and controls.”
- Do not: state scope details from memory; confirm via GRC.

### Evidence pointers (internal)
- Secure SDLC one-pager: /security-and-compliance/secure-sdlc/secure-development-lifecycle-summary
- Incident response one-pager: /security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/incident-response-and-notification-one-pager
- Standard RFP language: /sales-enablement/security-faq/standard-rfp-response-library

---

## Slide 2 — Shared Responsibility by Deployment Mode
### Recommended slide title
**Shared Responsibility: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- **Hosted API:** Redwood operates infra and service; customer controls app-layer security and access
- **Dedicated:** Dedicated compute capacity + isolation controls; shared operational responsibilities clarified per contract
- **Private (VPC/on‑prem):** Customer-controlled environment; Redwood provides software/control plane components as contracted

### Speaker notes
- “Most security questions become straightforward once we establish the boundary: what Redwood operates vs what the customer operates.”
- “Private deployments shift responsibilities (networking, underlying infrastructure controls, and some logging/monitoring integrations) into the customer’s environment, while Redwood provides the product capabilities and support model defined in the order form.”
- “If the customer has a specific control requirement (e.g., CMK/HSM, SIEM export, residency), we map it to the deployment mode that best satisfies it.”

### Common pitfall
- Do not say: “Private means Redwood has no access.”
- Say instead: “Access pathways and operational responsibilities are defined by the Private deployment architecture and the agreement; we can confirm details for your exact topology.”

---

## Slide 3 — Encryption (In Transit, At Rest, Key Management)
### Recommended slide title
**Encryption & Key Management**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- Encryption in transit (TLS for external endpoints)
- Encryption at rest for stored data
- Key management options vary by deployment mode (including customer-managed options for Dedicated/Private where applicable)

### Speaker notes
- “We use industry-standard encryption in transit for customer-facing endpoints. Data at rest is encrypted for supported storage systems used by the platform.”
- “For customers with stricter key control requirements, we support configurations and integrations that depend on the deployment mode. Dedicated and Private deployments typically offer the strongest alignment for customer-managed key requirements.”
- “If your policy requires specific cipher suites, certificate requirements, or customer-managed keys, we’ll validate the exact requirement against the deployment’s architecture and provide a written response.”

### Safe Q&A responses
- Q: “Do you support KMS/HSM?”
  - A: “We support key management integrations depending on deployment mode; we can confirm the supported options and boundaries for your target deployment.”
- Q: “Is prompt/output data encrypted?”
  - A: “Data is encrypted in transit; storage/retention behavior depends on configured features and deployment mode. We can walk through the data flow and retention controls.”

### Evidence pointers (internal)
- Refer prospect to the relevant one-pager pack for encryption (if included in the current pack) and to the Security FAQ v2 for approved wording.

---

## Slide 4 — Audit Logging (Console, API, Admin Actions)
### Recommended slide title
**Audit Logging & Monitoring (Who did what, when)**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- Audit logs for key administrative and access events (scope varies by deployment)
- Log categories: auth events, admin actions, configuration changes (as applicable)
- Export/integration options available for enterprise setups (confirm per deployment)

### Speaker notes
- “We provide audit logging for security-relevant actions in the Redwood Console and control plane (e.g., authentication-related events and administrative changes). The exact event types and export mechanisms depend on your deployment mode and plan.”
- “For enterprise customers, the goal is to make audit logs actionable: a customer can ingest events into their logging platform/SIEM and support investigations.”
- “If you need a sample schema or specific event names, we can provide the approved one-pager and, where appropriate, a sanitized example.”

### Do / Don’t
- Do: state the categories and that scope varies by deployment.
- Don’t: promise that “all API requests” or “all prompts/outputs” are logged. Logging of payloads is a separate requirement and is not implied by ‘audit logs.’

### Evidence pointers (customer-facing)
- Audit logging overview one-pager: /security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logging-overview-one-pager

---

## Slide 5 — SSO, SAML, SCIM & RBAC
### Recommended slide title
**Identity, SSO, and RBAC (Enterprise Access Controls)**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- SSO/SAML support for Redwood Console access (enterprise)
- Role-based access control (RBAC) for least privilege
- Provisioning automation (SCIM) where applicable (confirm availability)

### Speaker notes
- “For enterprise access control, we support SSO for the Console using SAML, and RBAC to enforce least privilege for admins and operators.”
- “Customers typically integrate Redwood with their IdP (Okta/Azure AD/etc.), enforce MFA via the IdP, and use RBAC to constrain actions.”
- “If SCIM provisioning is a requirement, we should confirm exact support and scope for the customer’s plan and deployment mode, and provide the approved one-pager language.”

### Common customer objections and responses
- “We need strict separation of duties.”
  - “RBAC supports assigning roles aligned to operational responsibilities; we can map your SoD policy to roles and provide an access model overview.”
- “We require centralized deprovisioning.”
  - “That’s typically achieved via IdP controls and provisioning automation; we’ll confirm the supported provisioning model for your setup.”

### Evidence pointers (customer-facing)
- SSO/SAML/SCIM one-pager: /security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sso-saml-and-scim-one-pager
- RBAC model reference (more detailed; share selectively): /security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-model-reference

## Slide 6 — Data Residency (Where data is processed and stored)
### Recommended slide title
**Data Residency & Regional Deployments**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- Region selection for supported deployments (availability depends on product and capacity)
- Residency posture differs by Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Clarify what data types may leave region (e.g., support operations) based on configuration and contract

### Speaker notes
- “Data residency is a top enterprise requirement and is highly dependent on deployment mode. Private deployments generally provide the strongest residency control because the customer runs in their environment. Dedicated provides more predictable isolation and regional control than shared Hosted.”
- “We distinguish between customer content (requests/responses), operational metadata (usage metrics), and logs/telemetry. The one-pager explains what is regional, what is configurable, and what is required for service operations.”
- “If a customer requires strict EU-only processing, we should confirm the exact region, logging configuration, and support access model in writing.”

### Do / Don’t
- Do: use the approved “data types” framing (content vs metadata vs logs).
- Don’t: state “no data leaves the region” unless explicitly confirmed for the specific deal configuration.

### Evidence pointers (customer-facing)
- Data residency one-pager: /security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/data-residency-one-pager

---

## Slide 7 — Data Retention & Deletion (Optional but recommended)
### Recommended slide title
**Data Retention & Deletion Controls**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- Retention defaults and configurable controls (where applicable)
- Customer deletion requests process
- Audit log retention considerations (separate from content retention)

### Speaker notes
- “Retention can mean different things: content retention (requests/responses), operational logs, and audit logs. We avoid implying that one setting covers all categories.”
- “We can provide the current defaults and which controls are configurable by deployment mode. If a customer needs a specific retention policy (e.g., 0 days content retention), we’ll validate the feasible configuration and capture it in writing.”

### Evidence pointers (customer-facing)
- Data retention controls one-pager: /security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/data-retention-controls-one-pager

---

## Slide 8 — How Evidence Sharing Works (Internal talking points; optional in customer decks)
### Recommended slide title
**Security Review Process (Questionnaires & Evidence Requests)**

### On-slide bullets (customer-safe)
- Standard security questionnaire support through Solutions Engineering + Security/GRC
- SOC 2 report and select evidence shared under NDA
- Defined turnaround and escalation path

### Speaker notes
- “To keep the process predictable, we route evidence requests through Security/GRC. Some artifacts require an NDA and controlled distribution.”
- “If you send us your questionnaire, we’ll respond with approved language and references to the relevant one-pagers; where evidence is requested, we’ll coordinate access.”

### Important
- Do not include internal links, internal SLAs, or named individuals’ direct emails on externally shared decks. Use the standard ‘security@’ channel or the AE/SE as the front door.

---

## Standard backup answers (for live Q&A)
### “Do you train on customer data?”
Use approved FAQ language. Default response in decks should be: “We do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models unless explicitly agreed otherwise in writing.” If unsure for a specific product feature, escalate to Security/GRC.

### “Can you support HIPAA/BAA / PCI / FedRAMP?”
Do not commit on a slide. Use: “We can discuss requirements and available options by deployment mode; any compliance commitments are contractual and may require specific configurations.”

### “Can we run fully on-prem / air-gapped?”
Use: “Private deployments include on‑prem options for certain regulated environments; feasibility and architecture depend on requirements. We’ll scope this with our Private deployments team.”

---

## Maintenance & ownership
- Canonical owner: Sales Enablement (Go-to-Market) with Security & Compliance PM approval.
- Review cadence: quarterly review, plus out-of-band updates when any of these change: audit log scope, residency regions, retention defaults, SSO/RBAC behavior, compliance scope.
- If you need to change wording: do not edit slides ad hoc. Open a request via the security appendix intake process and tag Naomi Feldman for review.

## Version history (summary)
- v2 (2026-02-12): aligned to Security FAQ v2; added explicit “avoid absolutes” guidance; clarified residency/retention framing; standardized audit logging disclaimers.
